Model & Results

A linear mixed model with random effect for individual and fixed effects of group, time and the interaction was run. Estimated marginal means were obtained, and contrasts specified to test Hypothesis 1 and Hypothesis 2.

This is the ANOVA table for the model. p-values are likelihood ratio tests for adding the new term to the model just before. A p-value <0.05 indicates that adding that term results in better model fit. The most important p-value is the interaction p-value. Here, there is evidence that the pattern of change over time is different among the groups (p=0.003).

Hypothesis 1

We hypothesize that from baseline (‘T1’) to post-treatment/waitlist (‘T2’) there will be a gradient effect, whereby parent-child dyads who receive PCIT-T will show the greatest gains and parent-child dyads who receive no treatment will show the least gains. For the outcome, then, the null hypothesis is:

\(H_0: \text {mean change}(\text{PCIT-T}) = \text {mean change}(\text{CoS-P}) = \text {mean change}(\text{Waitlist})\) \(H_A: \text {mean change}(\text{PCIT-T}) > \text {mean change}(\text{CoS-P}) > \text {mean change}(\text{Waitlist})\)

This is a joint hypothesis test.

First, confirming that the ordering of the means is as hypothesized:

## group = 1:
##  contrast estimate    SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  1 - 2       2.279 0.832 79.5   2.738  0.0206
##  1 - 3       1.436 1.039 82.7   1.382  0.3549
##  2 - 3      -0.843 1.054 78.3  -0.800  0.7042
## 
## group = 2:
##  contrast estimate    SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  1 - 2      -1.357 1.113 91.0  -1.220  0.4446
##  1 - 3       1.510 2.031 89.6   0.743  0.7384
##  2 - 3       2.867 2.068 83.4   1.386  0.3526
## 
## group = 3:
##  contrast estimate    SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  1 - 2      -1.739 0.791 76.6  -2.200  0.0775
##  1 - 3      nonEst    NA   NA      NA      NA
##  2 - 3      nonEst    NA   NA      NA      NA
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates

So, the mean change for PCITT > COSP > Waitlist.

Now, to get the p-value associated with the joint hypothesis.

##   (Intercept) group2 group3 time2 time3 group2:time2 group3:time2 group2:time3
## 1           0      0      0     0     0           -1            0            0
## 2           0      0      0     0     1            0            1            0
## 
##   General Linear Hypotheses
## 
## Linear Hypotheses:
##        Estimate
## 1 == 0   -3.636
## 2 == 0    2.583
## 
## Global Test:
##       F DF1 DF2  Pr(>F)
## 1 4.528   2 155 0.01227

p=0.0123. We have evidence that this the change from T1 to T2 is greater for G1 then G2 and the change in G2 is greater than in G3.

Hypothesis 2

Change from T2-T3

There will be a gradient of size of change from T2 to T3 such that the change in the PCIT-T group > the change in the CoS-P group. This isn’t really a gradient; it’s just 1 hypothesis.

First, the change in PCITT and COSP from time 2 to time 3:

## Specify contrast matrices
# Hyp1 is 1 df test
# could use alternative="less" ir alternative="greater" in glht
hyp2   <- matrix(c(0, 0,0, 0,0, -1,0,1 ),1)
hyp2F <- glht(result3, linfct = hyp2)
summary(hyp2F)
## 
##   Simultaneous Tests for General Linear Hypotheses
## 
## Fit: lmer(formula = outcome ~ group * time + (1 | id), data = dat)
## 
## Linear Hypotheses:
##        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
## 1 == 0   -3.710      2.314  -1.603    0.109
## (Adjusted p values reported -- single-step method)
s<-summary(hyp2F, test = Ftest())
#also see this webpage for more on contrasts https://rcompanion.org/rcompanion/h_01.html



## Extract pvaue for evidence / no evidence
evidence = ifelse(s$test$pvalue<0.05, "evidence", "no evidence")

Change in G1 from T2 to T3: -0.843

Change in G2 from T2 to T3: 2.867

p=0.1109. We have no evidence that the change from T1 to T3 is different for G1 and G2
